body_json.answer:
**Assessment:** rejected.

The new post's claim that large-scale immigration threatens national security closely echoes [T4-007195](#T4-007195), which argues that bringing people in would add to an existing "home grown terrorism" problem, and [T4-005893](#T4-005893), which frames illegal immigration as endangering "the safety of American children" while declaring "Illegal immigration is BAD!" [T4-007129](#T4-007129) offers a narrower, incident-based version of the security framing, describing an "illegal immigrant" making threats against the President and his wife, while [T4-006695](#T4-006695) shifts from threat claims to a policy demand for "that damn deportation force." The clearest difference is scope and framing: [T4-006133](#T4-006133) distinguishes "legal ways to immigrate" from "illegal ways," a distinction the new post's broad "large-scale immigration" language does not make, and none of the retrieved posts address the culture-threat element of the new post.
